headline: BPC-157 comes in
from the gray market.
dek: Men have used it for years, bought as ‘research use only.’ Now HHS lets pharmacies make it under ten conditions. Here’s what that changes, and what the research shows.

body: [[/bpc-157|BPC-157]] is a synthetic peptide, a chain of 15 amino acids copied from part of a protein found in human gastric juice.[^bpc] Men use it for injuries and recovery. A 2025 systematic review noted that, despite lacking FDA approval, “it is increasingly used by clinicians and athletes.”[^vasireddi] FDA’s review found it offered online “for research purposes only and not for human or veterinary use.”[^bpc]

How many men use it is not known; neither FDA’s review nor the HHS notice gives a count. FDA cited other signs: Google searches for BPC-157 at an all-time high in June 2024, more than 50 million views of tagged videos on YouTube and TikTok, and more than 100,000 members of peptide-related Reddit communities.[^bpc]

On October 30, 2026, a Department of Health and Human Services notice in the Federal Register said HHS “does not intend to take enforcement action against a State-licensed pharmacy, Federal facility, or licensed physician compounding a drug product using a peptide bulk drug substance found in Appendix A.”[^fr] BPC-157 is one of six peptides on that list, according to the law firm BakerHostetler, allowed under the skin, into muscle, by mouth or on the skin.[^baker] HHS gave its reasons: “based on the Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee meetings and data regarding utilization of peptides, HHS believes that there is significant interest in the use of these peptides in compounding given the lack of availability of approved products.”[^fr] It said it was acting “to expand and improve patient access.”[^fr]

BakerHostetler lists ten conditions. A licensed pharmacist or physician compounds the drug to the policy’s standards. The peptide matches the policy’s identity and route rules. It comes from an FDA-registered establishment with a valid certificate of analysis. Its manufacturer follows current good manufacturing practice. Each drug is made for a patient-specific prescription and holds a single listed active ingredient. Serious adverse events and quality problems are reported to FDA’s MedWatch program and state authorities. The label reads “This is a compounded drug product. Not for resale.”[^baker] Oral forms need records showing adequate absorption. Any device packaged with it is an FDA-cleared syringe. All other legal requirements, including sanitary conditions, apply. The policy does not cover products sold as research chemicals.[^baker]

For a man who uses BPC-157, the change is in the supply chain: a prescription in his name, a registered and tested source, a compounded-drug label, and a compounder required to report serious side effects.[^baker] Some of that goes beyond usual federal rules. FDA told its advisory committee in July that 503A compounders “are not required to report adverse events associated with compounded drug products to the FDA.”[^lash] The notice adds that “compounded drugs are not FDA-approved, which means FDA does not review their safety, effectiveness, or quality before they are marketed.”[^fr]

A product labelled for research has none of those conditions attached. In a statement on unapproved weight-loss drugs, FDA said products falsely labelled for research “have been sold directly to consumers for human use with dosing instructions”[^glp1] and are “of unknown quality.”[^glp1] On BPC-157 itself, FDA’s compounding safety page says “the agency lacks sufficient information to know whether the drug would cause harm when administered to humans.”[^fdarisk] One of three reports in FDA’s drug adverse-event database through December 2025 involved a research-labelled injection that also held [[/tb-500|TB-500]]; the woman’s skin and gums darkened, again on reuse. FDA judged the product a likely cause but could not separate the two peptides.[^bpc]

The research begins in animals. FDA summarized that “in rats, BPC-157-related substances could prevent colonic fistulas, hepatic lesions, and GI lesions induced by different challenges.”[^bpc] The 2025 review kept 36 studies, 35 of them animal or lab work, and reported that “in preclinical models, BPC-157 improved functional, structural, and biomechanical outcomes in muscle, tendon, ligament, and bony injuries.”[^vasireddi] FDA added that “its mechanisms of action remain poorly understood.”[^bpc]

In people, FDA’s search “yielded five clinical studies that utilized BPC-157.”[^bpc] Two Croatian studies survive as meeting abstracts: 24 healthy volunteers took rising enema doses for eight days, and a double-blind trial in 53 people with ulcerative colitis found no statistically clear difference from placebo in a disease score after two weeks.[^bpc] Three uncontrolled Florida studies followed. In a 2021 chart review, 11 of 12 knee-pain patients given BPC-157 injections reported significant improvement months later, though “no specific tools were used to measure their improvement.”[^knee] In a 2024 pilot, 10 of 12 women with interstitial cystitis reported complete symptom resolution after one bladder-wall injection.[^bladder] A 2025 pilot gave two adults IV doses and found no change in heart, liver, kidney, thyroid or blood-sugar markers.[^iv]

FDA noted that “no serious adverse events appear to have been reported with these studies,”[^bpc] and that they were short and small. Research has not yet reached the routes men use: “We found no studies that administered BPC-157 to humans via the proposed oral, SC, nasal, or transdermal ROA.”[^bpc] SC means under the skin; ROA means route.

FDA’s reviewers concluded that “a balancing of the criteria weighs against BPC-157 (free base) and BPC-157 acetate being placed on that list.”[^bpc] Healio reported that in July “the committee voted 8-6-1 twice to place BPC-157 free base and acetate forms on the list.”[^healio] FDA has not posted an official vote record. HHS says FDA’s rulemakings “may propose adding some or all of these peptides to the 503A bulks list based on the available evidence.”[^fr] It may revisit the interim policy if a safety signal arises.[^fr]

One trial is registered: NCT07437547, a Hudson Biotech Phase 2 study of whether the peptide “can speed structural healing and functional recovery after an acute grade II hamstring muscle strain.”[^nct437] About 120 people are planned; no results are posted.[^nct437] The same sponsor’s TB-500 entry, NCT07487363, opens: “This fictional study is an example of a ClinicalTrials.gov-style record.”[^nct487]

What is known: rat studies, five small human studies, and a new pharmacy route with ten conditions. What is not known: how many men use BPC-157, what it does in people by the routes they use, and what FDA will decide.
